1.0.0.en: 1 Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. 2 In the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity, 3 The word of the LORD came expressly unto Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the LORD was there upon him.

1.0.1.en: The prophet Ezekiel began his book by fixing the date of the first divine vision that was revealed to him, the place where he dwelt at that time, and the circumstances surrounding him.

1.0.2.en: He says: "Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year" [1]. Most probably he means that when he reached the age of thirty he became a priest, but without any priestly work. Perhaps he meant the thirtieth year from the time King Josiah began the movement of restoring the Temple and the religious reform; it is also possible that he meant the thirtieth year of the reign of Nabopolassar, the father of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the founder of the Babylonian Empire. Ezekiel was living on the banks of the Chebar canal at Tel Abib or near it (Ezek 3:15).

1.0.3.en: Ezekiel had reached the lawful age for taking up the priestly work: entering the sanctuary, offering sacrifices, taking part in the daily liturgies, celebrating the feasts and enjoying the joyful praises... But, sadly, he was deprived of all this because of the captivity, so he sat on the banks of the river Chebar weeping over the state of his country, his people and the temple of the Lord, as though he were repeating the psalm that says:

1.0.4.en: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion.

1.0.5.en: We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song of praise; and they that led us away captive said:

1.0.6.en: Sing us one of the songs of Zion.

1.0.7.en: How shall we sing the LORD's song in a strange land?!

1.0.8.en: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget..." (Ps 137).

1.0.9.en: Thus the soul of the priest was embittered, and the Spirit lifted him up to the heavens to bring him into the Jerusalem above and let him enjoy the eternal temple. So he does not see the ark of the covenant, the golden lampstand and the altar of incense... etc., but sees the fiery divine chariot and the fiery divine throne. The heavens were opened [1] that he might see the divine mysteries in a manner suited to the circumstances surrounding him, so that his soul might be filled with consolation, as he sees through them human nature, renewed by the fiery Holy Spirit and given to us in Christ Jesus our Lord through the waters of holy Baptism, having become a fiery chariot that carries God Himself!

1.0.10.en: The heavens were opened before the captive prophet Ezekiel that he might enter, as it were, to the throne of God Almighty, and realize that human affairs do not proceed at random but by a wonderful divine providence, for God, the Ruler of all, cares for everything that touches the life of man. This is the secret of our consolation in the midst of tribulation.

1.0.11.en: I see (heaven open); others do not see.

1.0.12.en: Let no one think that heaven is open in a simple material sense. Rather, we who sit here see the heavens open and closed according to our different degrees of worthiness. Perfect faith opens the heavens and doubt closes them.

1.0.13.en: St. Jerome: This first vision, which will be repeated, serves the following matters:

1.0.14.en: First: It consoles the broken soul of Ezekiel, that he might repeat the saying: "In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul" (Ps 94:19), "For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ" (2 Cor 1:5). For this reason the Apostle Paul probably saw Paradise while he was being stoned at Lystra, and the Apostle John was caught up to the Lord's day while he was exiled on the island of Patmos.

1.0.15.en: Second: The vision came to suit the circumstances surrounding the ministry, for God grants His vision and His gifts according to the needs of His generosity. When God met Moses, the first leader of the people, who was to bring them across from the state of harsh bondage into the wilderness, to bring them through Joshua into the land of freedom, He appeared to him in the form of the bush full of thorns, burning with fire and not consumed, to declare the mystery of the divine Incarnation, the suffering and the Resurrection. It is as though there is no beginning for the Church except through the work of salvation by the incarnate Christ, crucified and risen from the dead. The miracles that accompanied the prophet Moses came to confirm the same thing. Here, however, the spirit of the people was broken, especially since the Chaldeans were carrying the procession of the god Bel or Marduk through the streets of the capital in splendor and pomp, while this people were deprived of their temple and the songs of rejoicing had ceased among them; so their brokenness appeared as though it were the brokenness of their God. Therefore God did not reveal Himself in a simple burning bush but through the fiery chariot, full of glory and radiance, as though God wanted to assure His prophet and His people that His glory fills heaven and earth even in the moments in which He hands His people over to discipline by the hands of the Gentiles.

1.0.16.en: Third: This vision declares God's gift to human nature, which is sanctified by the divine Incarnation. The fiery chariot is the holy Church as a divine throne; it represents the universal Church, and it also represents the soul of the believer who has become a member of the Church of God and a burning fiery chariot that carries God within it, by receiving the Holy Spirit in the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Myron, and by surrendering its life into His hands that He may work in it continually.

1.0.17.en: Fourth: Perhaps God wanted to declare to the prophet Ezekiel what the servant of the Lord ought to be. If God is a consuming fire, so His servants also ought to be a flame of fire (Ps 104:4); they are made like the fiery chariot, so that by the fiery Holy Spirit they may be able to work for God. In this St. John Chrysostom says: [Whoever takes a leading role must be more radiant than a shining star, so that his life is without blemish, and all look to him and follow his example].

1.1.0.en: Fifth: Before the survey of the vision it is said: "and the hand of the LORD was there upon him" [3]. This phrase is very dear to the prophet Ezekiel, for if because of the captivity he was deprived of taking up the priestly work by inheritance, yet the hand of the Lord stretched out over him to bless him and entrust him with the spirit of prophecy... He is called by God directly to see the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, and to understand God's plan for all humanity through the generations until the end of the age. God appointed him for the service of the heavenly sanctuaries!

1.1.1.en: Sixth: In his first homily on the book of Ezekiel, Origen sees that Ezekiel here represents the Lord Christ at the moment of His Baptism. He truly became the son of man, and He is the true Word. He came to us, the captives, not that we might see the fiery chariot but that He might lead us by His Holy Spirit through the waters of Baptism, by the power of His Cross, to His divine throne. He opens His heavens before us, and we find for ourselves a place in the bosom of His Father, in which we settle and in which we rest forever. By His fiery Spirit He transforms His Church into a fiery chariot, and we all rise with our hearts to the throne of His grace, experiencing the pledge of His glory until we see Him face to face.

1.1.2.en: To understand these matters we need to enter briefly into some details of the vision, which included six things: the wind, the cloud and the fire; the four living creatures; the wheels; the firmament; the likeness of the throne and Him who sat upon it; and finally the rainbow. These carry mysteries concerning the heavenly life, the holy Church, and also the inner life of the believer, especially the servant of the Lord. Since the prophet in this chapter is trying to describe what cannot be described, he often repeats the word "likeness", as though human language, words and symbols could not help him to express what he saw.

1.2.s.en: 1. The wind, the cloud and the fire:

1.2.0.en: "And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire." [4].

1.2.1.en: Where the glory of the Lord is revealed, these three things often appear: the stormy wind, the great cloud and the continuous fire. These came together in power on the day of Pentecost in the upper room of Zion, when the Holy Spirit descended upon the disciples to establish the Church of the New Testament, for "suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them tongues as of fire, and it sat upon each of them, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit" (Acts 2:2-4). The stormy wind that filled all the house appeared as a sign of the Church's being filled with the divine Spirit; the continuous fire appeared through the tongues of fire that kindled the hearts of the believers with a divine fire that is not quenched; and the great cloud is the company of the disciples who were sanctified and became a cloud of witnesses for the Lord (Heb 12:1).

1.2.2.en: As for the stormy wind, we note that the word "wind ruah" in Hebrew is translated wind, spirit or breath according to the text. The connection between wind and spirit does not stop at the limits of the word, for the wind among the Jews was not merely a natural phenomenon, but often carried the meaning of the divine energy revealed in nature. In the Old Testament the divine presence was often linked with the stormy wind. The Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind (Job 28:1), and the Lord spoke to Moses "in the mountain out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice (stormy)" (Deut 5:22). And when Elijah stood on the mountain, "behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the LORD" (1 Kgs 19:11). For this reason the prophet Nahum says: "The LORD hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet" (Nah 1:3). And the psalmist says: "Our God shall come, and shall not keep silence: a fire shall devour before him, and it shall be very tempestuous round about him" (Ps 50:3).

1.2.3.en: St. Augustine comments on the psalmist's saying thus: [This without doubt makes a kind of separation. It is that separation which they do not expect, when the nets are torn before they bring them to land (Lk 5:6). In the separation a distinction is made between the righteous and the wicked]. It is as though the stormy wind took an eschatological meaning in the mind of St. Augustine. For as long as we are in this world, like fish in the net, the righteous are not separated from the wicked; but when it is brought to land, that is, to the great day of the Lord, the stormy wind separates these from those.

1.2.4.en: This separation or distinction that accompanies the coming of the great Lord takes place at present inwardly in the heart. On the feast of Pentecost, when the stormy wind blew, it gave the Church the spirit of discernment, not to condemn the wicked outside it but to judge spiritually within it, so that it separates the malicious one who clings to his malice from the simple and pure souls; and so that every member carries within himself the spirit of discernment that condemns the evil or the weakness into which he falls, walking in the light and fleeing from the darkness. He condemns himself and judges his inner depths, his actions and his conduct before he is judged.

1.2.5.en: In the book of Ezekiel, however, the prophet felt "a stormy wind coming from the north" [4], as though the Lord were affirming that He blows upon His people with the spirit of separation and discernment, to discipline them for their evil and to bring them, through captivity and suffering, into a pure life. The stormy wind or whirlwind comes from the north, and the north among the Jews signified distress and obscurity. Wherever the scorching north wind blows, plagues come and destruction occurs. While the false prophets were speaking smooth things (Isa 30:10), "saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 8:11), to calm the people's fears and to win the leaders to their side at the expense of the truth, the prophets spoke the truth even if it was wounding. This is what the prophet Ezekiel affirms: that God Himself is coming for discipline as in a northern stormy wind!

1.2.6.en: The Lord Christ linked the divine Spirit with the wind in a new theological understanding, saying: "The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit" (Jn 3:8). He revealed that the work of the Holy Spirit in the new birth through Baptism is a hidden, unseen work, yet its work and its effectiveness are perceived in the life of the believer. He blows like the stormy wind to shake the old foundations of the heart and raise up from it a new sanctuary. And the Spirit continues to blow always within us, not as one who comes from outside but as One who dwells in us, working for the growth of our new man; He works in us and we feel Him, but we do not grasp His mysteries. Thus the divine Spirit worked even in the Old Testament, through the discipline of the people coming from the north, in a hidden way that the people could not see, but it was the work of God in them after their return to Him.

1.2.7.en: As for the great cloud, from of old the divine presence has been linked with the cloud. When the people went out into the wilderness, the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them the way (Ex 13:21), and the Apostle Paul saw in this a type of the work of the Holy Spirit in Baptism (1 Cor 6:2), by which He brings us across from bondage to the freedom of the glory of the children of God. In more than one place, when Moses spoke with God, the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud (Ex 16:10; 19:9). And when Moses pitched a special tent outside the camp in which to meet with God, Scripture says: "the cloudy pillar descended, as Moses entered into the tabernacle, and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses. And all the people saw the cloudy pillar stand at the door of the tabernacle" (Ex 33:9-10). And when the tent of meeting was dedicated, "a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle" (Ex 40:34). And when the Temple was built in place of the tent of meeting, on the day of its dedication "the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD" (1 Kgs 8:11). And in the New Testament, when the Lord went up with three of the disciples on Mount Tabor and Moses and Elijah appeared, a bright cloud came and overshadowed them (Mt 17:5). And we read in the book of Revelation about the Lord's last coming: "Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him" (Rev 1:7). To what, then, does the cloud point?

1.2.8.en: A. The saints Cyril the Great, Augustine and Jerome see that the cloud is a symbol of the humanity of the Lord Christ, through which He appeared to us while the divinity was hidden from our eyes; and His appearing on the last day with the clouds means the hiding of the glory of His divinity from the wicked on the day of judgment, so that they do not enjoy it, while the righteous enjoy the glories of the incarnate God and His radiance is unveiled to them.

1.2.9.en: B. Pope Dionysius of Alexandria sees that the cloud points to the innumerable company of angels who appear surrounding the Lord on the day of His coming.

1.2.10.en: C. St. Augustine sees that the cloud points to the company of preachers, saying: "The word of God, who is Christ, will be in the cloud, that is, in those who preach the truth"; indeed he sees every member of the members of the Church as representing a cloud, in whom the Lord Christ comes, saying: "He comes now in His members as in the clouds, or He comes in the Church, which is the great cloud".

1.2.11.en: D. St. Ambrose sees that the cloud that overshadows the Church is the company of the prophets who present to her the person of the Lord Christ through their prophecies, saying: "Moses and Joshua were two clouds. Note that the saints are clouds", "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their houses?" (Isa 60:8). Isaiah and Ezekiel are as two clouds above me; the first showed me the holiness of the Trinity through the Cherubim and Seraphim. The prophets are all clouds, in which Christ came. He came in the Song of Songs in a clear and beloved cloud, shining with the joy of the Bridegroom (Song 3:11). He came in a swift cloud, incarnate of the Virgin, when the prophet saw Him coming as a cloud from the east (Isa 19:1). Rightly he called Him a swift (light) cloud, for there is in Him nothing of earthly attachments to weigh Him down".

1.2.12.en: E. Speaking of the bright cloud that appeared at the Transfiguration of the Lord Christ, Origen says: "Shall I dare to say that our Savior is also the bright cloud that overshadows the Gospel, the Law and the Prophets, since they received understanding? Those who saw His light in the Gospel, the Law and the Prophets".

1.2.13.en: As for the continuous fire, it is said of God Himself that He is a consuming fire (Heb 1:9), and His servants are also a flame of fire (Ps 104:4). So the appearing of the divine chariot in a continuous fire declares the presence of God, the burning Fire, who burns the thorns that choke the soul and at the same time grants it an inner illumination, that it may shine like lightning, so that it has "brightness, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire".

1.2.14.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem spoke of the fiery Holy Spirit in the human soul through Baptism, saying: [Why do you wonder?! Take an example from reality, though it is poor and commonplace, yet useful for the simple. If fire passes through a piece of iron, it makes it all fire; so one who was cold becomes burning, and if he was black he becomes shining. If fire, which is matter, penetrates iron in this way and works in it without hindrance, and it too is a body (matter), why do you wonder at the Holy Spirit that He penetrates the inner depths of the soul?!].

1.2.15.en: And St. John Chrysostom says: [Just as the power of fire, when it prevails over veins of raw gold mixed with the dust of the earth, turns them into pure gold, so, and even more than this, the Holy Spirit works in Baptism in those whom He washes, for He turns them into something purer than gold instead of clay. For when the Holy Spirit descends like fire in our souls, He first burns up the image of the earthy in order to give the image of the heavenly, so that it becomes like a bright, shining coin coming out of the furnaces of the smelter].

1.2.16.en: St. Augustine comments on the psalmist's words: "A fire goeth before him" (Ps 97:3), saying: [Are you afraid? Let us be changed and we shall not fear! Let the straw fear the fire, but what does the fire do to gold?!]. He also comments on the phrase: "For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried" (Ps 66:10) thus: [Not to burn us with fire like stubble but like silver. By the use of fire You do not turn us into ashes but wash us from defilement].

1.3.0.en: 5 Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man. 6 And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings. 7 And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot: and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass. 8 And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they four had their faces and their wings. 9 Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went; they went every one straight forward. 10 As for the likeness of their faces, they four had the face of a man, and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle. 11 Thus were their faces: and their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies. 12 And they went every one straight forward: whither the spirit was to go, they went; and they turned not when they went. 13 As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps: it went up and down among the living creatures; and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning. 14 And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.

1.3.1.en: We have already spoken about these heavenly beings and said that they are the two orders of the Cherubim (Kerubim) and the Seraphim, and we pointed to the dignity of this creation, its work, its form and what it signifies, at some length in our interpretation of the fourth chapter of the book of Revelation; but we add here the following:

1.3.2.en: A. In the book of Revelation St. John saw one face for each living creature, so that he saw in the four only four faces. The prophet Ezekiel, however, says that he saw four faces for each living creature, a face on each side. Perhaps the reason is that the former looked at this creation from one side, while the latter looked at it from all sides, since he saw the chariot in a state of movement in every direction.

1.3.3.en: These faces, as St. John Chrysostom sees them, point to the intercession of these spiritual beings for the human race (like the face of a man), for the beasts of the wilderness (the likeness of the face of a lion), the animals of the field (the likeness of the face of an ox) and the birds of heaven (the likeness of the face of an eagle), because they are beings nearer to God, to whom be glory, than the rest of the heavenly spiritual beings.

1.3.4.en: If we take the interpretation of St. Gregory of Nazianzus and Origen, we see in the fiery chariot the soul sanctified with all its powers to carry the divine throne: the lion points to the irascible power, the ox to the appetitive, the man to the rational (the mind), and the eagle to the spiritual. This is the work of the Holy Spirit in the soul: He enkindles our powers with His fire, not to destroy them but to sanctify them and make them complete together, so that we become like a fiery chariot that carries God in it!

1.3.5.en: If we take the interpretation of St. Victorinus and Irenaeus, we see in these faces a reference to the four Gospels, which bring the soul into salvation, so that it enjoys the Kingdom not as something outside itself but within it, and it becomes itself a sanctuary for the Lord.

1.3.6.en: If we take the interpretation of St. Jerome, we see that the secret of our bearing God, the consuming Fire, lies in our enjoyment of divine salvation through the Incarnation (the likeness of the face of a man), the crucifixion (the ox), the Resurrection (the lion) and the Ascension (the eagle). By this mystery, the mystery of the incarnate God, crucified, risen from the dead and ascended into the heavens, the soul sets out as a fiery chariot to carry within it, by the Holy Spirit, the divine life.

1.3.7.en: Finally, if these four beings represent the holy Church that carries the divine life within her, then these four are the episcopate, the presbyterate, the diaconate, and the people. They are the principal pillars that work together for the Lord Christ; any difference in one of the pillars makes the Church lose her balance and harms her message. If a pillar loses its work or its interaction with the other pillars, the whole loses its vitality; for the Church is not centered on a bishop, a priest, a deacon or a lay official (from the people), but is a life that is integrated and interacting together.

1.4.0.en: B. Each creature appears with four wings, whereas in the book of Revelation each creature has six wings. Perhaps the difference results from the appearance of what the prophet Ezekiel called the firmament over the heads of the living creatures, as though each living creature had lifted two wings above its head in the form of a dome to shield its eyes from the radiance of God's majesty, so that the two raised wings did not appear but the other four. So the soul that enjoys the life of fellowship with God, especially the servant of the Lord, becomes like a cherub with six wings: it covers itself with two wings, flies toward God with two wings, and hides its eyes with the other two wings from the radiance of His majesty! The prophet Ezekiel noticed that the wings of the Cherubim are joined one to another [9]; so if the cherub represents the highest heavenly order, then its holy life, burning with fire, does not accept bearing the divine throne, as a secret, except by its union with the life of others. Perhaps this is what led St. Macarius the Great to say: [That a person's salvation is in the lives of others, for he cannot enjoy salvation isolated from his brother but only as a member with him in the one body of the one Head].

1.4.1.en: C. Their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like burnished brass [7]. The straight feet represent the uprightness of the spiritual man, who has two feet like burnished brass, which tread the earth and crush the thorns, and sparkle with the radiance of heavenly things without being soiled by the dust of the world. The true believer walks upon the world without fear, directed toward heaven without being entangled in temporal things.

1.4.2.en: D. "And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides" [8]. The spiritual man lives flying in the heavenly places as with the wings of the Spirit, and his hands are always ready to work for the Kingdom of God, to serve every human being! He has wings as well as hands! Perhaps the presence of the hands under the wings means that the heavenly beings worship God and serve men; they have the spirit of worship and service together!

1.4.3.en: E. "Their wings were joined one to another" [9], that is, all worship together in a spirit of love, harmony and unity.

1.4.4.en: F. Also the prophet looked at these living creatures and saw their faces on every side, as though they had no back, able to move in every direction without turning [9]; as though they had no back, for it is fitting for one who bears the divine throne, having entered into the fullness of glory, not to have a back, but to be all faces and all eyes, ever looking to God without hindrance. Therefore, when the people sinned against God, He rebuked them, saying: "they have turned unto me the back, and not the face" (Jer 2:27). This is the expression that He used more than once on the lips of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer 7:24; 18:17; 32:33), and it is as though the prophet Ezekiel came to complete the words of the prophet Jeremiah in another style: instead of rebuking them for offering the back and not the face, he stirs them to imitate this heavenly creation, so that they have no back at all but their life in the Lord is all faces and meetings with Him!

1.5.0.en: The prophet describes their movement, saying: "whither the spirit was to go, they went" [12]. For the Holy Spirit is the One who leads the divine procession; He leads the heavenly ones and the earthly ones sanctified in the truth. He repeats the word "went" to confirm the necessity of our commitment to walk according to the plan of the Holy Spirit and under His leadership, without deviation to the right or to the left.

1.6.0.en: G. The prophet saw the living creatures constantly moving in a harmonious way, like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of lamps of fire, and something like lightning went forth from them [13]. It is a living picture of the work of God in us, who makes us ever moving toward Him; He enkindles us and makes us a burning fire, and enlightens us so that we become like lightning, filled with Him in radiance. We move by the fiery, holy Spirit!

1.6.1.en: H. The sound of their movement is fearful, like the sound of many waters, like the sound of an army.

1.6.2.en: This is the work of God in our lives: He makes of the soul a mighty army that Satan and all his forces cannot overcome. For this reason St. Cyril of Jerusalem says to the candidates for Baptism: [Each one of you comes and presents himself before God, in the presence of the innumerable hosts of angels, and the Holy Spirit places a seal upon your souls. By this you enroll yourselves in the army of the great King]. And Father Theodore of Mopsuestia says: [Now you have been chosen for the Kingdom of Heaven, and you can be recognized. If anyone examines you, he will find you a soldier of the King of heaven].

1.6.3.en: I. In the tenth chapter the prophet Ezekiel called the living creature a cherub. And, remarkably, the cherub is closely linked with our salvation: he appeared in the first of the books of the Bible holding a sword burning with fire, guarding the way to Paradise so that man should not enter to the tree of life, since fallen human nature cannot approach the mystery of life; and he appeared in the last of the books of the Bible with the twenty-four heavenly presbyters sharing in the song of the Lamb, which is the song of our salvation (Rev 5:9), since man has been given the right to enter heaven itself, his nature having been glorified in Christ Jesus, the true Lamb. And between the beginning of the Bible and its end two cherubim also appear on the ark of the covenant in the tent of meeting and the Temple as a sign of the divine presence, and God used to speak with Moses from between them. The presence of two cherubim above the ark of the covenant, which represents the throne of God, points to God who dwells in the midst of His people speaking with them and dealing with them through mercy and love. The presence of two also points to the role of the heavenly ones toward us: praying for us and working as servants for those who are about to inherit salvation (Heb 1:14). And the drawing of the form of the cherub on the curtains of the Tabernacle and the veil (Ex 25-26), nearer to the form of a winged man, declares the drawing near of human nature to the divine presence.

1.6.4.en: Man came to know the cherub, so that he became not a stranger to humanity; therefore the Gentiles knew him, especially the Chaldeans, although they added to him forms of their own devising, as all the nations did with all the truths of the faith that they received orally by tradition and tinted with their distorted thought.

1.6.5.en: So when we see the cherub we remember our human nature, which enjoyed salvation through its union with God in Christ Jesus our Lord by His Holy Spirit. His four faces point to the sanctification of our new nature in all its aspects: the intellectual (man), the spiritual (the eagle), work (the ox) and authority (the lion).

1.6.6.en: J. St. Clement of Alexandria followed Philo the Jew, saying: [The word "cherub" means "knowledge", as though through spiritual knowledge our life becomes a chariot that carries God within it]. This was also accepted by St. Jerome, who saw in the cherub a symbol of the storehouse of knowledge that works in our nature to lift it up and set out with it among the heavenly powers. It works in our nature, ruling over the desires like a lion, soaring in the heavenly things like an eagle, laboring with striving like the ox and with discretion like a man. We draw this knowledge from the four Gospels, for the same saint says: [Matthew, Mark, Luke and John are the Lord's four-fold team, the true Cherubim, or storehouse of knowledge; for their body is full of eyes and shines like lightning..., their feet are straight and lifted up, their back winged, ready to fly in every direction, each of them holding on to the other, interlaced one with another, like wheels in the midst of wheels rolling along the line, moving according to the breathings of the Holy Spirit].

1.7.0.en: K. "And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning" [14]. Perhaps he thereby points to the service of the heavenly ones who are sent to us but quickly run to return to where the divine throne is, enjoying the vision of God. And the true believer whose heart is kindled with longing for his Savior, from time to time his heart and mind run, and all his senses run, to return like lightning, enjoying contemplation of their Savior. It cries out with the Apostle: "I have a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better" (Phil 1:23).

1.8.0.en: "15 Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold one wheel upon the earth by the living creatures, with his four faces. 16 The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel. 17 When they went, they went upon their four sides: and they turned not when they went. 18 As for their rings, they were so high that they were dreadful; and their rings were full of eyes round about them four. 19 And when the living creatures went, the wheels went by them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up. 20 Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went, thither was their spirit to go; and the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels. 21 When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up over against them: for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels." [15-20].

1.8.1.en: A. What are these wheels upon the earth, which carry within them the spirit of the living creatures, and which move in harmony with them, and at the same time are lifted up, and dreadful, and full of eyes, their appearance like the colour of a beryl, a wheel in the middle of a wheel? St. Jerome answers: [The two wheels are the New and Old Testaments, for the Old moves in the New, and the New moves in the Old]. And he gives proof of this from what is said in the tenth chapter: "As for the wheels, it was cried unto them in my hearing, Gelgel" [(Ezek 10:13) the Septuagint]; for the word Gelgel is different from the word Gilgal, which means rolling (Deut 11:30) or a circle, since the former is made of two words "gal gal" which mean "revelation". It is as though the voice that the prophet Ezekiel heard coming from the wheels was "the revelation of the New Testament and the revelation of the Old Testament". For the two Testaments are joined together for the purpose of declaring the mystery of the salvation of mankind through Christ Jesus, the center of the Gospel. In this St. Ambrose says: [The prophet saw a wheel running in the midst of a wheel. This vision certainly does not refer to a bodily matter but to the grace of the two Testaments. The wheel in the midst of the wheel is life under the Law and life through grace. As long as it is within the Church, grace has contained the Law]. And St. John Chrysostom says: [The two Testaments are bound together and joined one with the other; the Old Testament reveals the mysteries of the New Testament and makes them clear through types and prophecies, and the New Testament reveals the mysteries of the Old Testament that were hidden behind the shadows].

1.8.2.en: He saw the wheels upon the earth, but their rings were high and dreadful, as though the word of God, presented in the two Testaments, came down to us through our human language so that we might understand it and live it while we are here on earth, and at the same time it is lifted up and dreadful, lifting the soul to the heavenly places and entering into the mysteries full of awe and trembling. As St. John Chrysostom says: [One who has been granted the effectiveness of the word of God cannot remain in this present lowliness, but rather seeks for himself two wings with which he may set out to the high places, discovering the light of the boundless good things].

1.8.3.en: B. The wheels are linked with the earth, for the fiery chariot is linked with us human beings, so that it may carry us from the dust of this world to the fiery heavenly life.

1.8.4.en: It is the chariot of God, of whom it is said that His way is in the sanctuary and His way is in the sea (Ps 77:13, 19), the God of heaven and earth together; the whole world glorifies Him.

1.8.5.en: C. The link of the wheels with the earth confirms that God is the Ruler of history and its Maker; He is the One working in all ages... The wheel of His love and care for the sons of men keeps turning without stopping... even if man does not understand its mysteries and wisdom!

1.8.6.en: D. As for its appearance, it was like the appearance of a beryl, a kind of very hard precious stone of a light green colour, and it is the tenth stone on the breastplate of the high priest (Ex 28:20), by which he enters the sanctuaries of God. It is as though God grants the soul hardness and strength to face all the wars of Satan; the light green colour points to the fruits it produces in the life of man, for it makes his heart a joyful paradise; and its presence on the breast of the high priest reveals the work of the Word in us, for He makes our names engraved upon the breast of the Lord Christ, the Bishop of our souls, who is in the bosom of His Father, interceding for us by His blood to bring us in to the bosom of His Father. Finally, this stone is one of the stones that adorn the foundations of the walls of the new Jerusalem (Rev 21:20)... as though the word of God were the secret of the adornment of the bride, who enjoys entering the bridal chamber of the Bridegroom forever!

1.8.7.en: So the word of God is the precious stone of great price which the priest, the monk and the people ought to acquire, as the secret of victory, triumph, union with the Lord Christ and entrance into the heavenly life. Therefore, when Father Ignatius Brianchaninov wrote his book "The Arena of Martyrdom", presenting a method for the monastic life from the Fathers of the Church, he began it by directing the monks' eyes to Holy Scripture and the Gospel commandments, saying: [The early holy monks called the monastic life the life according to the commandments of the Gospel], and St. John Climacus defines the monk thus: The monk is the one who is led by the commandments of God and the word of God at every time, in every place and in every matter. The monks who were subject to St. Pachomius the Great were obliged to learn the Gospel by heart, so that the law of the incarnate God might be like a book always open in the memory, seen constantly by the eyes of the soul, imprinted on the soul so that they might fulfill it easily and without failure. The blessed Elder Seraphim of Sarov says: [We must train ourselves so that the mind is immersed in the law of the Lord, which guides and governs our life].

1.9.0.en: E. "And their rings were full of eyes round about them four" [18]. The spiritual man carries the spirit of discernment and wisdom, full of eyes...

1.9.1.en: These rings are high and dreadful [18]; the spiritual man is marked by spiritual loftiness, so that he is counted in the eyes of heaven as high and honored... He is so high that the enemy of good cannot catch him, and dreadful because the Spirit of God who is in him is greater than all satanic powers.

1.10.0.en: 22 And the likeness of the firmament upon the heads of the living creature was as the colour of the terrible crystal, stretched forth over their heads above. 23 And under the firmament were their wings straight, the one toward the other: every one had two, which covered on this side, and every one had two, which covered on that side, their bodies. 24 And when they went, I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of great waters, as the voice of the Almighty, the voice of speech, as the noise of an host: and when they stood, they let down their wings. 25 And there was a voice from the firmament that was over their heads, when they stood, and had let down their wings.

1.10.1.en: "And the likeness of the firmament upon the heads of the living creatures was as the colour of the terrible crystal, stretched forth over their heads above" [22].

1.10.2.en: He saw upon the heads of this living heavenly creation the likeness of the firmament of heaven (the dome) in the form of a canopy. So when the believer presents all his bodily, intellectual, psychological and spiritual powers as holy instruments of righteousness to the Lord, his life is transformed into the likeness of a heavenly canopy that overshadows his inner heart.

1.10.3.en: In this St. John Saba says: [Behold, heaven is within you if you are pure, and the angels in it you see shining], [The kingdom of the pure of soul is within his heart, and the sun that rises in it is the light of the Holy Trinity, and the air of its breeze is the Holy Spirit the Comforter, and those who dwell with him are the spiritual natures of the pure ones, and their life, their joy and their delight is Christ, the radiance of the Father].

1.10.4.en: As for the firmament's having the appearance of the terrible crystal stretched forth, this is because the nature of crystal is that it reflects within itself the scene before it, as though it were a mirror; so the scene of the Lord who is carried above the firmament is reflected within the believer. That is, the soul, having become a heaven for the Lord and a sanctuary for Him, has become like the crystal that bears His image and reflects His features in it. This scene reminds us of what St. John saw: "And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal" (Rev 4:6), and Bishop Victorinus sees that this sea points to Baptism, for everyone who desires to meet Him who sits upon the throne must pass through this sea, so that the grace of God penetrates his soul and it is prepared for the Kingdom. As for its being like crystal, it is because it is fitting that the baptized be steadfast and strong.

1.10.5.en: As the rays of Him who sits on the throne, the Sun of Righteousness, are reflected on the crystal sea, the colors of the spectrum appear clearly upon the living creatures, that is, the many and varied gifts and endowments of God appear in the life of the believers.

1.11.s.en: 5. The throne and Him who sat upon it:

1.11.0.en: "26 And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it. 27 And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about." [26-27].

1.11.1.en: When the life of the believer is transformed into a heavenly canopy, the different colors are reflected upon it through the likeness of the crystal, and the throne of God appears upon it, and within it the incarnate Word of God appears as a King enthroned upon the heart. He is like the appearance of a man and at the same time like the colour of amber; from His loins upward kindled with fire, and from His loins downward filled with brightness. Thus the Lord appears to us with the burning fire that consumes all evil in us, and with the radiance that He pours upon our inner depths, so that our inner sight is opened and is filled with glory. He draws near to us for our reconciliation, so He burns in us the works of the old man and fills us with radiance through the new man!

1.11.2.en: St. Gregory the Theologian saw the mystery of the divine Incarnation revealed through this vision, and said: [This God-bearing chariot is the holy Virgin Mary, whom the Holy Spirit overshadowed, so she became glorified and filled with virtues].

1.12.0.en: 28 As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake.

1.12.1.en: Where the divine throne appears we see a rainbow around it (Rev 4:3), because the glory of God is not only might and majesty but also boundless love. The rainbow is the sign of love that God gave when He made a covenant with Noah after the Flood (Gen 9), and God remains, as the One who loves mankind, offering us all love through His covenant with us. This bow has many colors that declare God's many kindnesses and gifts to us. And as a bow it points to the bow used in wars, as though God defends us with His bow, but without an arrow because He does not love the shedding of blood; by it we overcome sin and trample upon Satan.
